newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Chandra Asri denies Petronas talk.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Chandra Asri denies Petronas talk.

text.p: Indonesia's privately-owned PT Chandra Asri Petrochemical Centre on Thursday denied reports that a major shareholder was preparing to sell his stake in the firm to Malaysian state oil company Petronas.
Chandra Asri CEO Peter Gontha said in a statement that the reports were baseless.
Bisnis Indonesia daily reported this week that timber tycoon Prajogo Pangestu was in talks with Petronas to sell down his stake in the company, Indonesia's only olefin producer.
"This affront .. is offensive to the company, our shareholders and to Indonesia's achievement," Gontha said.

"Mr. Pangestu is still with Chandra Asri as our operations continue to settle down, our customer base grows and we study ways in which we can add components to further enhance our contributions to developing the downstream potential for Indonesia's petrochemical industry," he said.
Petronas has also denied that it is in talks with Pangestu.

Chandra Asri, before changing its status to a foreign investment company, was 40 percent owned by Pangestu, 25 percent by Indonesian businessman Henry Pribadi and 35 percent by President Suharto's Bambang Trihatmodjo.
Following the changes, Hong Kong-based investment companies Siemene International and Stallion Co Ltd hold 65 and 10 percent respectively while Japan Indonesia Petrochemical Corp holds the rest.
Bisnis Indonesia said Pangestu currently holds a 10 percent stake in Chandra Asri through the investment companies while Trihatmodjo holds 60 percent.
Chandra Asri has an annual production capacity of around 520,000 tonnes of ethylene, 243,000 tonnes of propylene, 300,000 tonnes of polyethylene and purolysis gasoline.
